concepts.title: 1. Translating Text to Equations
concepts.subtitle: Define variables and identify independent conditions
concepts.summary: Define the unknowns with units and translate two independent conditions into a pair of linear equations.

points.text: Define: Assign x and y to the requested unknown quantities.
Translate: Convert one condition into one equation at a time.
Keep meanings fixed: Interpret the final values using the original definitions.

concepts.trap: Changing variable meanings or translating only part of a verbal condition.

concepts.title: 2. Number and Digit Problems
concepts.subtitle: Use place value explicitly
concepts.summary: For a two-digit number with tens digit x and units digit y, use 10x+y; reversal gives 10y+x.

points.text: Tens digit contributes ten times its value.
Units digit contributes its value once.

concepts.trap: Treating x+y as the number itself or reversing without swapping place values.

concepts.title: 3. Fixed and Variable Costs
concepts.subtitle: Separate constant and quantity-dependent charges
concepts.summary: Model total cost as a fixed charge plus quantity multiplied by a unit charge.

points.text: Unit charge is multiplied by quantity.

concepts.trap: Confusing an observed total with the fixed charge.

concepts.title: 4. Speed, Distance, Time and Boats
concepts.subtitle: Distinguish downstream and upstream speeds
concepts.summary: Use distance = speed × time together with downstream x+y and upstream x-y relations.

points.text: Keep distance, time, and speed units consistent.

concepts.trap: Adding stream speed upstream or confusing distance with speed.

concepts.title: 5. Fraction Adjustments and Geometric Dimensions
concepts.subtitle: Translate ratios and dimensions before solving
concepts.summary: Cross-multiply changed fractions carefully and translate rectangle dimensions using perimeter relations.

points.text: Define numerator/denominator or length/breadth with units.

concepts.trap: Reversing numerator and denominator or forgetting the factor 2 in perimeter.

worked_examples.title: Type 1: Age relationship
worked_examples.problem: Five years ago, Nuri was three times as old as Sonu. Ten years from now, Nuri will be twice as old as Sonu. How old are they now?

steps.statement: Let Nuri's present age be x years and Sonu's present age be y years.
steps.calculation: \begin{aligned}\text{Nuri's present age} &= x \\ \text{Sonu's present age} &= y\end{aligned}
steps.reason: Defines the unknown present ages.
Past ages are five years less than present ages.
Future ages are ten years more than present ages.
The variables represent the present ages.

worked_examples.conclusion: Nuri is 50 years old and Sonu is 20 years old.

worked_examples.title: Type 2: Two-digit reversal
worked_examples.problem: A two-digit number has digits whose sum is 11. The number is 27 greater than its reversal. Find the number.

steps.statement: Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y.
steps.reason: Uses place value.
The digits add to the stated sum.
The original number exceeds its reversal by 27.

steps.statement: Solve the digit pair and reconstruct the number.
steps.reason: Place the tens digit before the units digit.

worked_examples.title: Type 3: Fixed and variable cost
worked_examples.problem: A service has a fixed charge and a unit charge. Four units cost ₹35 and nine units cost ₹60. Find both charges.

steps.statement: Let the fixed charge be x rupees and the unit charge be y rupees per unit.
steps.reason: Defines the two pricing components.
Fixed charge plus four unit charges gives the observed cost.
The same model applies to nine units.
Subtracting the observations removes the fixed charge.

worked_examples.conclusion: The fixed charge is ₹15 and the unit charge is ₹5.

worked_examples.title: Type 4: Upstream and downstream
worked_examples.problem: A boat travels 40 km downstream in 2 hours and 24 km upstream in 2 hours. Find the still-water speed and stream speed.

steps.statement: Let still-water speed be x km/h and stream speed be y km/h.
steps.reason: Defines the two unknown speeds.
Distance divided by time gives downstream speed.
Distance divided by time gives upstream speed.

steps.statement: Solve and interpret x and y.
steps.reason: These are the still-water and stream speeds.

worked_examples.conclusion: Still-water speed is 16 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h.

worked_examples.title: Type 5: Rectangle dimensions
worked_examples.problem: The length of a rectangle is 11 cm more than its breadth. Its perimeter is 74 cm. Find the dimensions.

steps.statement: Let length be x cm and breadth be y cm.
steps.reason: Defines the dimensions.
Length exceeds breadth by 11 cm.
Uses the rectangle perimeter formula.
The variables represent length and breadth.

worked_examples.conclusion: The rectangle is 24 cm long and 13 cm broad.

pool.statement: A service has a fixed charge plus a variable charge per unit. 3 units cost ₹35, while 7 units cost ₹55. Find the fixed charge and the charge per unit.

steps.strategy_question: Which variable definition matches the two unknown pricing components?
strategy_options: Let fixed charge be x rupees and variable charge be y rupees per unit.
Let quantity be x and total cost be y.
Let fixed charge be y and variable charge be x, without units.
Let fixed charge be ₹35 and variable charge be y.

option_details.text: Let fixed charge be x rupees and variable charge be y rupees per unit.
option_details.explanation: Correct! The two unknown pricing components become x and y.

option_details.text: Let quantity be x and total cost be y.
option_details.explanation: Both quantity and cost are given for the observations, so they are not the unknowns.

option_details.text: Let fixed charge be y and variable charge be x, without units.
option_details.explanation: Swapping variables without tracking units makes interpretation error-prone.

option_details.text: Let fixed charge be ₹35 and variable charge be y.
option_details.explanation: ₹35 is a total observed cost, not necessarily the fixed charge.

steps.calc_prompt: Enter the two unit meanings for x and y.
steps.rubric_text: Keep rupees and rupees-per-unit distinct.
steps.rubric_math: \begin{aligned} \text{Fixed charge} &= x \\ \text{Variable charge per unit} &= y \end{aligned}
steps.hint: Use x for the fixed charge and y for the variable charge.

steps.strategy_question: Which equation models the 3-unit observation?

option_details.explanation: Correct! The fixed charge appears once and the variable charge is multiplied by the quantity.
The quantity coefficient belongs with y, not x.
This reverses the meanings of fixed and variable costs.
A positive usage quantity adds to the fixed charge, rather than subtracting.

steps.calc_prompt: Enter the quantity coefficient and observed total cost.
steps.rubric_text: Use fixed charge plus quantity times variable charge.
steps.hint: Multiply the per-unit charge by the number of units, then add the fixed charge.

steps.strategy_question: Which equation models the 7-unit observation?

option_details.explanation: Correct! The second observation uses its own quantity and total cost.
The second quantity must replace the first quantity.
The coefficient belongs to the variable charge, not the fixed charge.
The second observation has a different total cost.

steps.calc_prompt: Enter the quantity coefficient and observed total cost.
steps.rubric_text: Repeat the same cost model using the second observation.
steps.hint: Use the second quantity and its corresponding observed total.

steps.strategy_question: Which final strategy correctly identifies both pricing components?
strategy_options: Subtract the two cost equations to remove the fixed charge, then interpret the remaining values.
Add the equations to double the fixed charge.
Treat the total cost as the variable charge per unit.

option_details.text: Subtract the two cost equations to remove the fixed charge, then interpret the remaining values.
option_details.explanation: Correct! Subtraction removes the common fixed charge and leaves a one-variable equation.

option_details.text: Add the equations to double the fixed charge.
option_details.explanation: Adding keeps the fixed charge instead of eliminating it.
One observation cannot determine both pricing components.

option_details.text: Treat the total cost as the variable charge per unit.
option_details.explanation: A total cost includes both fixed and variable parts.

steps.rubric_text: Subtract to eliminate x, solve for y, then substitute to find x.
steps.hint: The difference in total cost divided by the difference in quantity gives the per-unit charge.
